title: Vegan diets: practical advice for athletes and exercisers
publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
claims: The ISSN broad protein recommendation of 1.4-2.0 g/kg/day is described as appropriate for most athletic contexts; endurance-sport athletes are commonly cited at 1.2-1.4 g/kg/day and strength or power athletes at 1.6-1.7 g/kg/day.

Plant-based protein sources are often incomplete in essential amino acids and typically contain less branched-chain amino acids than animal-based equivalents; lysine is the limiting amino acid in many cereal grains.
Leucine appears to be a primary trigger of muscle protein synthesis; plant proteins are often low in leucine, while soy beans and lentils are cited plant sources of leucine.
Vegetarians may need to consume more protein than meat eaters to compensate for poorer digestibility of plant sources; vegan athletes may aim toward the higher end of the 1.4-2.0 g/kg/day range.

The older recommendation to combine plant protein sources within a single feeding to achieve a complete essential amino acid profile is no longer considered necessary; a variety of grains, legumes, nuts and seeds across the diet provides the essential amino acids.
